title: Three Curriculum Tracks
panelPrompt: Click a track to see what students at that level are working on.

image.style: flat vector comparison poster, clean geometric icons, muted textbook palette, generous white space
image.overall: A three-column comparison poster about coding club curriculum levels. Each column is a tall rounded panel with a coloured header bar carrying its printed title, and simple flat icons below. The three printed headers, and the ONLY text in the image, are: "Beginner Track", "Intermediate Track", "Advanced Track".
image.layoutNotes: Divide the content area into 3 equal-width vertical columns with a thin pale divider line or a clear gutter of background between each pair. Every column must have the SAME width, the SAME top edge, and the SAME bottom edge, so the overlay's rectangular hover zones line up with them exactly. Each column has its printed header in bold dark text at the very top of the column, on a tinted header bar in that column's accent colour. Below the header, fill the column with simple flat ICONS and abstract shapes only -- no words, no bullet points, no sentences. Leave a clear margin of at least 4% of the image width on the left and right edges and 8% of the height at the top and bottom.

zones.label: Beginner Track
facts: First Scratch sprite and block-coding projects
Heavy use of unplugged coding activities to build vocabulary before screens
Success measured by finishing and sharing one complete project

draw.position: The left column, roughly 2% to 32% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted blue. Below it: a keyboard icon, two interlocking puzzle-piece code blocks, and a small cat-like sprite shape.

zones.label: Intermediate Track
zones.summary: The block-to-text transition and core Python.
facts: Python variables, loops, and conditionals introduced one at a time
Turtle graphics challenges provide visual verification
Peer code review starts here, as students have enough code to review

draw.position: The centre column, roughly 35% to 65% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted amber. Below it: a puzzle-piece block on the left with an arrow pointing right to a plain text-line icon, plus a small turtle shape trailing a simple spiral path.

zones.label: Advanced Track
facts: Combines functions, loops, and conditionals into a single project like a simple game
Pair programming and live coding demonstrations become regular practice
Students often begin serving as peer mentors (Chapter 9) themselves
Strongest fit for professional mentor involvement

draw.position: The right column, roughly 68% to 98% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted mint green. Below it: several small code-block shapes assembling into one larger rounded shape, plus two figures side by side at one screen suggesting pair programming.

quiz.question: Which track introduces Python variables and loops one at a time?
Which track uses unplugged activities to build vocabulary before screens?
In which track do students often start peer mentoring?
